record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: If such an integer N(k) exists for k-monomial one-variable complex polynomials, determine N(k) exactly or provide a good upper bound for it.

evidence.quote: Problem 27. (ii) If the answer is yes, ﬁnd N(k) or a good upper bound of this number.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer k. Say that a polynomial f ∈ ℂ[x] is k-monomial if it has at most k nonzero coefficients, i.e. f(x) = Σ_{j=1}^{k} a_j x^{n_j} for some complex coefficients a_1,…,a_k and nonnegative integer exponents n_1,…,n_k. For f ∈ ℂ[x] and i ≥ 0, define the i-th moment of f by
   m_i(f) := ∫_0^1 f(x)^i dx.
Suppose it is known that there exists a positive integer N = N(k), depending only on k, with the following property: for every k-monomial polynomial f ∈ ℂ[x],
   if m_i(f) = 0 for every i ∈ {0, 1, 2, …, N(k)}, then m_i(f) = 0 for every i ≥ 0.
Determine the exact value of the smallest such N(k), or give a good explicit upper bound for it as a function of k.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches confirm the question originates from a 2021 list of open problems in low-dimensional dynamical systems by A. Gasull, and is closely related to the polynomial moment problem (Briskin–Françoise–Yomdin, Pakovich) and to fewnomial-type counts. No source was found reporting either an exact value of N(k) or an explicit upper bound for it in the k-monomial one-variable setting; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: Compilation of open problems including a section on problems involving polynomials, with a moments-type problem related to the Jacobian conjecture and to Kouchnirenko's fewnomials conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in 2020/2021 with no resolution provided.

status_evidence.title: Moment vanishing problem and positivity: Some examples (Pakovich et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies vanishing of moments of polynomials and the polynomial composition condition; treats the general (two-polynomial) polynomial moment problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature treats general moment-vanishing problems but does not provide an explicit N(k) for k-monomial single polynomials.
